annotationRationale: The solution uses the signs of odd and even powers and the parity of the number of negative factors. It also preserves the distinction between a positive range and the separate open intervals formed by removing every root.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Algebra is correct; no repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The positive intervals are (1,2), (2,3), (5,6), (6,7), (9,10) and (10,infinity), giving 6, choice C. All ten roots are removed, producing the stated eleven intervals. The stem, choices and key agree; no figure contradiction exists.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: 2023_AMC_10B_Q12/count-negative-odd-factors is retained and independently verified for the same polynomial and ordered choices. The supplied sign-flipping and graph descriptions express the same parity mechanism, so another route is unnecessary.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed power-sign and product-sign nodes are both central. The interval splitting is derived explicitly and needs no additional catalog node.
review.areaCheck: Algebra is correct; no repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Away from the removed roots, even powers are positive and odd powers preserve their bases' signs. The five-factor product has respectively 5,4,3,2,1,0 negative factors on the listed ranges. Its three positive ranges split at the original roots 2,6,10, yielding exactly six positive intervals.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The explanation accurately reuses 2023_AMC_10B_Q12/count-negative-odd-factors and retains its inherited aops-reference-2023_AMC_10B_Q12 ID. Project reuse and third-party mathematical influence are honestly labeled source-informed-original; no official argument is claimed.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The rule x<k explains every table entry. The distinction between the sign of the simplified product and the intervals remaining after every original root is removed is particularly clear.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_020 covers odd/even power signs, and cnm_015 covers the parity of negative factors in a product. Both are directly used.
